// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	auth_model "gitea.dev/models/auth"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"
	issue_service "gitea.dev/services/issue"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestMilestoneBurndown(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	t.Run("Data", func(t *testing.T) {
		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, session, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)

		due := time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, 7)
		req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/milestones", api.CreateMilestoneOption{
			Title: "burndown", Deadline: &due,
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		milestone := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Milestone{})

		indexes := make([]int64, 0, 2)
		for _, title := range []string{"first", "second"} {
			req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues", api.CreateIssueOption{
				Title: title, Milestone: milestone.ID,
			}).AddTokenAuth(token)
			indexes = append(indexes, DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Issue{}).Index)
		}
		closed := "closed"
		req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues/%d", indexes[0]), api.EditIssueOption{
			State: &closed,
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)

		// anyone who can read the repository's issues can read its burndown
		req = NewRequest(t, "GET", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/milestone/%d/burndown", milestone.ID))
		burndown := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), &issue_service.MilestoneBurndown{})

		require.Len(t, burndown.Points, 1, "a milestone made today has one day of history")
		today := burndown.Points[0]
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Remaining)
		assert.Equal(t, 2, today.Scope)
		assert.Equal(t, issue_service.BurndownInsufficientData, burndown.Status)
		require.NotNil(t, burndown.Ideal)
		assert.Equal(t, today.Date, burndown.Ideal.From)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, burndown.Ideal.FromValue)
		assert.Equal(t, burndown.Deadline, burndown.Ideal.To)

		// the chart and the progress bar above it must count the same thing
		row := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Milestone{ID: milestone.ID})
		assert.Equal(t, row.NumIssues-row.NumClosedIssues, today.Remaining)
		assert.Equal(t, row.NumIssues, today.Scope)
	})

	t.Run("NotFound", func(t *testing.T) {
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/milestone/99999/burndown"), http.StatusNotFound)
		// milestone 4 belongs to repo 42, so it cannot be read through repo 1
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/milestone/4/burndown"), http.StatusNotFound)
	})

	t.Run("PrivateRepoHidden", func(t *testing.T) {
		// user2/repo2 is private, so a signed-out reader learns nothing about its milestones
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo2/milestone/1/burndown"), http.StatusNotFound)
	})

	t.Run("IssuesAndPullsDisabled", func(t *testing.T) {
		// user13/repo11 enables the code unit only, so it has no milestone pages to chart
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user13/repo11/milestone/1/burndown"), http.StatusNotFound)
	})
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-05 20:12:17Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>

```text
## Conventions & invariants

- Filenames are PascalCase and match the component name.
- **Components do not mount themselves.** A `features/` module does it, guarded by the presence of
  its root element:

  ```ts
  const el = document.querySelector('#repo-contributors-chart');
  if (!el) return;
  createApp(RepoContributors, {repoLink: el.getAttribute('data-repo-link')}).mount(el);
  ```

  So adding a component always means touching `frontend-js.md`'s wiring too.
- Props come from `data-*` attributes read with `getAttribute`, or from `window.config.pageData`
  (set by the handler via `ctx.PageData`, see `templates.md`). Do not fetch configuration the
  server could have handed you.
- Show and hide with `v-if` / `v-show` — not `.tw-hidden`, which is the plain-JS mechanism.
- **Do not mix Vue with Fomantic-UI JavaScript.** Fomantic's CSS classes are fine; its jQuery
  behaviours fight Vue's ownership of the DOM.
- No JSX — SFCs only.
- Data fetching still goes through `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts`.
- Logic worth testing is pulled into a sibling `.ts` file and tested there; the `.vue` file stays
  presentational. `ActionRunView.ts` beside `RepoActionView.vue` is the pattern.

## Recipes

**Add a component.** Create `YourThing.vue`, a mount block in the owning `features/` module,
a root element with the data attributes it needs in the template, and — if it has real logic — a
sibling `.ts` with a `.test.ts`.

**Give a component server data.** Small values as `data-*` attributes on the mount point; anything
structured via `ctx.PageData` in the handler, read as `window.config.pageData`.

**Test one.** `pnpm exec vitest <name>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- A component with no mount call is dead code that still ships in the bundle — the compiler will
  not tell you.
- `.ts` files in this directory are not components; they are stores and extracted logic. Do not
  assume everything here is a `.vue`.
- Because mounting is element-guarded, a typo in the root element's id or class fails silently:
  nothing renders and nothing errors.

## Related

```typescript
// mirrors MilestoneBurndown in services/issue/milestone_burndown.go
export type BurndownStatus = 'empty' | 'done' | 'closed' | 'projected' | 'not_burning' | 'insufficient_data';

export type BurndownPoint = {
  date: string, // "YYYY-MM-DD" in the instance's zone, used as is so every viewer sees the same day
  remaining: number,
  scope: number,
};

export type MilestoneBurndown = {
  points: BurndownPoint[],
  deadline: string,
  ideal: {from: string, fromValue: number, to: string} | null,
  status: BurndownStatus,
  projected: string,
  daysLate: number | null,
  completedOn: string,
};

export type BurndownSummaryLocale = {
  statusDone: string,
  statusClosed: string,
  statusNotBurning: string,
  statusInsufficient: string,
  projected: string,
  projectedOnTime: string,
  projectedOnDueDate: string,
  projectedLate: string,
};

export type LinePoint = {x: string, y: number};

// fills %s and %d in order, the way the server-side locale strings are written
export function formatLocale(template: string, ...args: Array<string | number>): string {
  let next = 0;
  return template.replace(/%[sd]/g, () => String(args[next++]));
}

// the one-line verdict above the chart; it carries the late or early state in words, not only in colour
export function burndownSummary(data: MilestoneBurndown, locale: BurndownSummaryLocale): string {
  switch (data.status) {
    case 'done':
      return formatLocale(locale.statusDone, data.completedOn);
    case 'closed':
      return locale.statusClosed;
    case 'not_burning':
      return locale.statusNotBurning;
    case 'insufficient_data':
      return locale.statusInsufficient;
    case 'projected':
      if (data.daysLate === null) return formatLocale(locale.projected, data.projected);
      if (data.daysLate > 0) return formatLocale(locale.projectedLate, data.projected, data.daysLate);
      if (data.daysLate === 0) return formatLocale(locale.projectedOnDueDate, data.projected);
      return formatLocale(locale.projectedOnTime, data.projected, -data.daysLate);
    default:
      return '';
  }
}

export function idealLine(data: MilestoneBurndown): LinePoint[] {
  if (!data.ideal) return [];
  return [{x: data.ideal.from, y: data.ideal.fromValue}, {x: data.ideal.to, y: 0}];
}

// from today's remaining work down to zero on the projected day
export function projectionLine(data: MilestoneBurndown): LinePoint[] {
  if (data.status !== 'projected' || data.points.length === 0) return [];
  const today = data.points[data.points.length - 1];
  return [{x: today.date, y: today.remaining}, {x: data.projected, y: 0}];
}

// the axis must reach the due date and the projected finish, or their lines are cut off
export function burndownAxisMax(data: MilestoneBurndown): string {
  // ISO dates sort as strings
  const dates = [data.points[data.points.length - 1].date, data.deadline, data.projected].filter(Boolean);
  return dates.reduce((latest, date) => (date > latest ? date : latest));
}

import {burndownAxisMax, burndownSummary, formatLocale, idealLine, projectionLine, type MilestoneBurndown} from './RepoMilestoneBurndown.utils.ts';

const locale = {
  statusDone: 'Completed on %s',
  statusClosed: 'closed',
  statusNotBurning: 'not burning',
  statusInsufficient: 'insufficient',
  projected: 'Projected %s',
  projectedOnTime: 'Projected %s, %d early',
  projectedOnDueDate: 'Projected %s, on the day',
  projectedLate: 'Projected %s, %d late',
};

function burndown(fields: Partial<MilestoneBurndown>): MilestoneBurndown {
  return {
    points: [{date: '2026-01-05', remaining: 3, scope: 3}, {date: '2026-01-06', remaining: 2, scope: 3}],
    deadline: '',
    ideal: null,
    status: 'projected',
    projected: '',
    daysLate: null,
    completedOn: '',
    ...fields,
  };
}

test('formatLocale', () => {
  expect(formatLocale('%s then %d', 'a', 2)).toEqual('a then 2');
  expect(formatLocale('no placeholders')).toEqual('no placeholders');
});

test('burndownSummary', () => {
  expect(burndownSummary(burndown({status: 'done', completedOn: '2026-01-06'}), locale)).toEqual('Completed on 2026-01-06');
  expect(burndownSummary(burndown({status: 'closed'}), locale)).toEqual('closed');
  expect(burndownSummary(burndown({status: 'not_burning'}), locale)).toEqual('not burning');
  expect(burndownSummary(burndown({status: 'insufficient_data'}), locale)).toEqual('insufficient');
  expect(burndownSummary(burndown({status: 'empty'}), locale)).toEqual('');

  expect(burndownSummary(burndown({projected: '2026-01-09'}), locale)).toEqual('Projected 2026-01-09');
  expect(burndownSummary(burndown({projected: '2026-01-09', daysLate: 3}), locale)).toEqual('Projected 2026-01-09, 3 late');
  expect(burndownSummary(burndown({projected: '2026-01-09', daysLate: 0}), locale)).toEqual('Projected 2026-01-09, on the day');
  // early is sent as negative days late and read back as a positive count
  expect(burndownSummary(burndown({projected: '2026-01-09', daysLate: -4}), locale)).toEqual('Projected 2026-01-09, 4 early');
});

test('idealLine', () => {
  expect(idealLine(burndown({}))).toEqual([]);
  expect(idealLine(burndown({ideal: {from: '2026-01-05', fromValue: 3, to: '2026-01-10'}}))).toEqual([
    {x: '2026-01-05', y: 3},
    {x: '2026-01-10', y: 0},
  ]);
});

test('projectionLine', () => {
  expect(projectionLine(burndown({status: 'not_burning'}))).toEqual([]);
  expect(projectionLine(burndown({projected: '2026-01-08'}))).toEqual([
    {x: '2026-01-06', y: 2},
    {x: '2026-01-08', y: 0},
  ]);
});

test('burndownAxisMax', () => {
  expect(burndownAxisMax(burndown({}))).toEqual('2026-01-06');
  expect(burndownAxisMax(burndown({deadline: '2026-01-10'}))).toEqual('2026-01-10');
  expect(burndownAxisMax(burndown({deadline: '2026-01-10', projected: '2026-01-14'}))).toEqual('2026-01-14');
  // a due date already passed does not pull the axis back
  expect(burndownAxisMax(burndown({deadline: '2026-01-01'}))).toEqual('2026-01-06');
});

```vue
<script lang="ts" setup>
import {SvgIcon} from '../svg.ts';
import {
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Tooltip,
  LinearScale,
  TimeScale,
  PointElement,
  LineElement,
  type ChartOptions,
  type ChartData,
} from 'chart.js';
import {GET} from '../modules/fetch.ts';
import {Line} from 'vue-chartjs';
import {chartJsColors} from '../utils/color.ts';
import {errorMessage} from '../modules/errors.ts';
import 'chartjs-adapter-dayjs-4/dist/chartjs-adapter-dayjs-4.esm';
import {computed, onMounted, shallowRef} from 'vue';
import {
  burndownAxisMax,
  burndownSummary,
  idealLine,
  projectionLine,
  type BurndownSummaryLocale,
  type MilestoneBurndown,
} from './RepoMilestoneBurndown.utils.ts';

const {pageData} = window.config;

Chart.defaults.color = chartJsColors.text;
Chart.defaults.borderColor = chartJsColors.border;

Chart.register(
  TimeScale,
  LinearScale,
  Legend,
  Tooltip,
  PointElement,
  LineElement,
);

const props = defineProps<{
  locale: BurndownSummaryLocale & {
    loadingTitle: string;
    loadingTitleFailed: string;
    loadingInfo: string;
    title: string;
    remaining: string;
    scope: string;
    ideal: string;
    projection: string;
    empty: string;
    noDeadline: string;
  };
}>();

const isLoading = shallowRef(false);
const errorText = shallowRef('');
const burndown = shallowRef<MilestoneBurndown | null>(null);

const hasChart = computed(() => burndown.value !== null && burndown.value.status !== 'empty');
const summary = computed(() => (hasChart.value ? burndownSummary(burndown.value!, props.locale) : ''));

onMounted(() => {
  fetchBurndown();
});

async function fetchBurndown() {
  isLoading.value = true;
  try {
    const response = await GET(pageData.milestoneBurndownLink!);
    if (response.ok) {
      burndown.value = await response.json();
      errorText.value = '';
    } else {
      errorText.value = response.statusText;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    errorText.value = errorMessage(err);
  } finally {
    isLoading.value = false;
  }
}

function toChartData(data: MilestoneBurndown): ChartData<'line'> {
  // dash patterns tell the lines apart without relying on their colours
  const late = data.daysLate !== null && data.daysLate > 0;
  return {
    datasets: [
      {
        label: props.locale.remaining,
        data: data.points.map((p) => ({x: p.date, y: p.remaining})),
        borderColor: chartJsColors.commits,
        backgroundColor: chartJsColors.commits,
        borderWidth: 2,
        pointRadius: data.points.length > 60 ? 0 : 2,
        pointHitRadius: 6,
        stepped: 'after', // work drops when an item closes, not gradually between closes
        order: 0,
      },
      {
        label: props.locale.scope,
        data: data.points.map((p) => ({x: p.date, y: p.scope})),
        borderColor: chartJsColors.border,
        backgroundColor: chartJsColors.border,
        borderWidth: 1,
        borderDash: [4, 4],
        pointRadius: 0,
        pointHitRadius: 6,
        stepped: 'after',
        order: 1,
      },
      {
        label: props.locale.ideal,
        data: idealLine(data),
        borderColor: chartJsColors.text,
        backgroundColor: chartJsColors.text,
        borderWidth: 1,
        borderDash: [6, 4],
        pointRadius: 0,
        pointHitRadius: 0,
        order: 2,
      },
      {
        label: props.locale.projection,
        data: projectionLine(data),
        borderColor: late ? chartJsColors.deletions : chartJsColors.additions,
        backgroundColor: late ? chartJsColors.deletions : chartJsColors.additions,
        borderWidth: 2,
        borderDash: [2, 3],
        pointRadius: 0,
        pointHitRadius: 6,
        order: 3,
      },
    ].filter((dataset) => dataset.data.length !== 0),
  };
}

function toChartOptions(data: MilestoneBurndown): ChartOptions<'line'> {
  return {
    responsive: true,
    maintainAspectRatio: false,
    animation: false,
    interaction: {
      mode: 'nearest',
      intersect: false,
    },
    plugins: {
      legend: {
        display: true,
      },
      tooltip: {
        callbacks: {
          // show the server's own date string, not one the browser re-derived in the viewer's zone
          title: (items) => (items[0].raw as {x: string}).x,
        },
      },
    },
    scales: {
      x: {
        type: 'time',
        min: data.points[0].date,
        max: burndownAxisMax(data),
        grid: {
          display: false,
        },
        time: {
          unit: 'day',
          parser: 'YYYY-MM-DD',
        },
        ticks: {
          maxRotation: 0,
          maxTicksLimit: 10,
        },
      },
      y: {
        beginAtZero: true,
        ticks: {
          maxTicksLimit: 6,
          precision: 0,
        },
      },
    },
  };
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="milestone-burndown">
    <div class="tw-flex tw-items-baseline tw-justify-between tw-flex-wrap tw-gap-2">
      <strong>
        {{ isLoading ? locale.loadingTitle : errorText ? locale.loadingTitleFailed : locale.title }}
      </strong>
      <span v-if="hasChart" class="milestone-burndown-summary">
        {{ summary }}<template v-if="!burndown!.deadline"> {{ locale.noDeadline }}</template>
      </span>
    </div>
    <div class="tw-flex ui segment burndown-graph">
      <div v-if="isLoading || errorText !== '' || !hasChart" class="tw-m-auto">
        <div v-if="isLoading">
          <SvgIcon name="gitea-running" class="tw-mr-2 rotate-clockwise"/>
          {{ locale.loadingInfo }}
        </div>
        <div v-else-if="errorText !== ''" class="tw-text-red">
          <SvgIcon name="octicon-x-circle-fill"/>
          {{ errorText }}
        </div>
        <div v-else class="tw-text-text-light">
          {{ locale.empty }}
        </div>
      </div>
      <div v-else class="tw-w-full" role="img" :aria-label="summary">
        <Line :data="toChartData(burndown!)" :options="toChartOptions(burndown!)"/>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.burndown-graph {
  height: 260px;
}
</style>

```

export async function apiCreateIssue(
  requestContext: APIRequestContext,
  {owner, repo, title, body, projects, headers}: {
    owner: string;
    repo: string;
    title: string;
    body?: string;
    projects?: number[];
    headers?: Record<string, string>;
  },
): Promise<{index: number}> {
  let result: {index: number} = {index: 0};
  await apiRetry(async () => {
    const response = await requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues`, {
      headers: headers || apiHeaders(),
      data: {title, body: body || '', projects: projects || []},
    });
    if (response.ok()) {
      const json = await response.json();
      // API returns "number" field for the issue index
      result = {index: json.number};
    }
    return response;
  }, 'apiCreateIssue');
  return result;
}
export async function apiCreateRepo(requestContext: APIRequestContext, {name, autoInit = true, headers}: {name: string; autoInit?: boolean; headers?: Record<string, string>}) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/user/repos`, {
    headers: headers || apiHeaders(),
    data: {name, auto_init: autoInit},
  }), 'apiCreateRepo');
}

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import {login, apiCreateRepo, apiCreateIssue, apiCreateMilestone, apiDeleteRepo, assertNoJsError, randomString} from './utils.ts';

test('milestone burndown charts remaining work against the ideal line', async ({page}) => {
  const repoName = `e2e-burndown-${randomString(8)}`;
  const user = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
  await Promise.all([login(page), apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repoName})]);
  const dueOn = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
  const {id} = await apiCreateMilestone(page.request, {owner: user, repo: repoName, title: 'Sprint', dueOn});
  await Promise.all([
    apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner: user, repo: repoName, title: 'First', milestone: id}),
    apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner: user, repo: repoName, title: 'Second', milestone: id}),
  ]);

  await page.goto(`/${user}/${repoName}/milestone/${id}`);
  const chart = page.locator('#milestone-burndown-chart');
  await expect(chart.locator('canvas')).toBeVisible();
  // one day of history is too little to project, and the summary says so in words
  await expect(chart.locator('.milestone-burndown-summary')).toContainText('two days of history');
  await expect(chart.locator('[role="img"]')).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', /two days of history/);

  await assertNoJsError(page);
  await apiDeleteRepo(page.request, user, repoName);
});

test('milestone burndown shows an empty state without items', async ({page}) => {
  const repoName = `e2e-burndown-empty-${randomString(8)}`;
  const user = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
  await Promise.all([login(page), apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repoName})]);
  const {id} = await apiCreateMilestone(page.request, {owner: user, repo: repoName, title: 'Empty'});

  await page.goto(`/${user}/${repoName}/milestone/${id}`);
  const chart = page.locator('#milestone-burndown-chart');
  await expect(chart).toContainText('This milestone has no issues or pull requests yet.');
  await expect(chart.locator('canvas')).toBeHidden();

  await apiDeleteRepo(page.request, user, repoName);
});
EOF

# models/issues — issues, pull requests, comments, reviews

**Read when:** querying or changing issue, PR, comment, label, milestone or review rows.
**Not here:** the business logic on top -> `services/issue` and `services/pull`; project boards -> `models/project`.

## Responsibilities

One package for the whole issue domain, because pull requests *are* issues in this schema.
`models/pull` is separate and tiny: automerge scheduling and per-user review state.

| Area | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Issue core | `issue.go`, `issue_list.go`, `issue_update.go`, `issue_search.go`, `issue_stats.go` |
| Pull requests | `pull.go`, `pull_list.go` |
| Comments | `comment.go`, `comment_list.go`, `comment_code.go`, `content_history.go` |
| Reviews | `review.go`, `review_list.go` |
| Labels / milestones | `issue_label.go`, `label.go`, `milestone.go`, `milestone_list.go` |
| People / time | `assignees.go`, `stopwatch.go`, `tracked_time.go` |
| Relations / state | `dependency.go`, `issue_xref.go`, `issue_watch.go`, `issue_pin.go`, `issue_lock.go`, `issue_user.go`, `issue_project.go`, `reaction.go` |

| `models/issues/issue_group.go` | `IssueLabelGroup`, `IssueList.GroupByExclusiveLabelScope` — the grouped list view |

  kinds.

## Gotchas

- Counter columns on `Repository` (`NumIssues`, `NumClosedIssues`, `NumPulls`, ...) are
  denormalised. Changing issue state means keeping them in step, and fixture rows must match or
  `unittest.CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
- `Issue.Index` and `PullRequest.Index` are both present. They agree, but write through the issue.
- `Issue.Link()` dereferences `issue.Repo`, so an issue fetched with `GetIssueByID` panics there
  until `LoadRepo(ctx)` has run.
- `models/pull` is not "pull requests" — those are here in `models/issues/pull.go`. `models/pull`
  is only automerge and review state.
- `GroupByExclusiveLabelScope` and `applyGroupByLabelScope` (`models/issues/issue_search.go`, driven
  by `IssuesOptions.GroupLabelScope`) derive the same groups twice — once in SQL to keep a page's
  rows contiguous, once in Go to split that page. Their ordering rules must stay identical, and
  both tie-break on `label.id`, never `label.name`: SQL collation does not match Go's string
  comparison, so a name tie-break silently disagrees across a page boundary.

## Related

- `models-db.md` — transactions and `GetNextResourceIndex`
- `models-repo-and-git.md` — the counter columns and repo units that gate issues

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.

**Known limitation:** a hand-edit to a guide that only rewords prose is not mechanically
detectable. Rule 21 catches invented facts; rule 18 catches a stale guide; review catches the rest.

## Updating `verified-at`

`verified-at` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against, from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Bump it whenever you confirm or correct a doc. A doc whose `verified-at` is far behind `main` has
not been checked recently — treat its details as hints and confirm them in the code before relying
on them.

58	
59	| Where | What it is for |
60	| --- | --- |
61	| `models/issues/issue.go` | The `Issue` struct itself, its loaders, and its "not found" error. |
62	| `models/issues/issue_list.go` | `IssueList` — a slice of issues that can load everything for all of them at once. |
63	| `models/issues/pull.go` | The pull-request-only row. |
64	| `models/issues/comment.go` | Comments, and the enum of comment kinds. |
65	| `models/issues/issue_close_reason.go` | Why an issue or pull request was closed: the `CloseReason` values and their names, which ones each kind may use, which ones the list's bulk Close offers, which one the close button starts on, and the check that refuses a bad one. Saved in three columns on `Issue`. |
66	| `models/issues/issue_label.go` | Labels on issues — and the clearest small example of the loader pattern. |
67	| `models/issues/issue_index.go` | Recalculating per-repository numbering. |
68	| `models/issues/issue_group.go` | Splitting a list of issues into category groups, for the grouped ("folder") list view. |
69	
70	The rest divide by area: `review.go` and `review_list.go`, `label.go`, `milestone.go`,
71	`assignees.go`, `stopwatch.go` and `tracked_time.go`, and the relationship files `dependency.go`,
72	`issue_xref.go`, `issue_watch.go`, `issue_pin.go`, `issue_lock.go`, `reaction.go`.
73	
74	## The rules, and why
75	
76	**`IsPull` decides what a row is.** A query that forgets it returns both issues and pull requests.
77	On an issues page that means pull requests appearing in the list; on a count, a number that is
78	always too high.
79	
80	**`Index` is not `ID`.** `ID` is the global primary key. `Index` is the number in the URL, unique
81	only *within* a repository — so every repository has an issue `#1`. Looking something up from a URL
82	means matching on the repository **and** the index. Using the URL number as an `ID` finds a
83	completely unrelated issue in another repository, which is worse than an error because it looks like
84	it worked.
85	
86	**Never set `Index` yourself.** It comes from the shared numbering helper, called inside the same
87	transaction that inserts the row. Assigning it by hand races with anyone else creating an issue in
88	that repository at the same moment.
89	
90	**Fields tagged `xorm:"-"` are empty until you load them.** `Repo`, `Poster`, `Labels`,
91	`Milestone`, `Assignee`, `Attachments`, `Comments`, `PullRequest` and others are all filled in by a
92	matching `LoadXxx(ctx)` method. `LoadAttributes(ctx)` loads the usual set in one go.
93	
94	**Loaders never refresh.** Each is guarded by an internal "already loaded" flag, so calling one
95	twice is free — but it also means a value that changed in the database after the first call **stays
96	stale on that struct**. If you need current data, re-fetch the issue; calling the loader again does
97	nothing.
98	
99	**Errors come in three parts.** There is an `ErrIssueNotExist` struct, an `IsErrIssueNotExist(err)`
100	test, and an `Unwrap()` that returns a shared sentinel like `util.ErrNotExist`. That third part is
101	what lets a handler ask "is this a not-found error?" without importing every model package — and it
102	is what turns a missing issue into a 404 instead of a 500.
103	
104	**Comment kinds are an enum**, and rendering branches on it. A plain comment and a review are both
105	comments with different kinds, as are all the "closed this", "added a label" timeline entries.
106	Adding a kind means handling it in the templates too, or it renders as nothing.
107	
108	**Extra data on a comment goes in its metadata, not a new column.** `Comment` has a JSON field,
109	`CommentMetaData`, and its code comment in `comment.go` asks for any new non-index data to go there.
110	It is written once, when the comment is created, and never changed — which suits a timeline, where
111	each entry records what was true at that moment. The cost is that SQL cannot search, sort or index
112	on anything inside it.
113	
114	**A close reason travels as a word, not a number.** The database stores each reason as a number,
115	but forms and pages send its name instead: `not_planned`, not `2`. `CloseReason.String` turns a
116	reason into its name and `AsCloseReason` turns a name back, the same way `CommentType.String` and
117	`AsCommentType` work for comment kinds. Because pages send these names, a name can no more be
118	changed than its number can.
119	
120	**A close comment keeps its own copy of the reason.** The issue's reason describes the *current*
121	close; the comment's copy, in `CommentMetaData`, describes *that* close and never changes. Read it
122	with `Comment.MetaCloseReason()` rather than reaching into the metadata yourself: close comments
123	written before this feature existed have no metadata at all, and the method turns that into "no
124	reason" instead of an error.
125	
126	**A duplicate is typed as a number but stored as an ID.** Closing as a duplicate of `#12` looks
127	`#12` up in the issue's own repository (`GetIssueByIndex`, inside `SetIssueAsClosed`), so a number
128	from another repository is refused. What gets stored is that issue's global ID. `Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue` turns the ID back into the
129	issue, repository included; if the target has since been deleted, it reports "not found" instead
130	of breaking the page.
131	
132	**Reopening wipes the issue's reason, not the comment's.** `setIssueAsReopen` is the only code that
133	reopens anything, and it clears the reason, text and duplicate target on the issue. The close
134	comment keeps what was true when it was written.
135	
136	## How to actually do it
137	
138	**Display a list of issues.** Fetch into an `IssueList`, then call `LoadAttributes(ctx)` **once, on
139	the list**. That type exists precisely to load everything for every issue in a handful of queries.
140	Looping and calling the single-issue loader is the N+1 it was built to prevent, and it is the
141	difference between a fast page and a slow one.
142	
143	**Add a column to `Issue`.** Add the field with its tag, write a migration, and if the value
144	duplicates something stored elsewhere, extend the consistency check in `models/main_test.go` and the
145	fixtures.
146	
147	**Get the pull request for an issue.** `issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx)`, then read `issue.PullRequest`.
148	Going the other way, use the pull request's own loader and then `pr.Issue`.
149	
150	## Traps, and what they look like
151	
152	**A field is empty and you are sure it has data.** You did not call its loader. There is no error
153	for this — the field is simply the zero value. Check for the `LoadXxx` call before you check the
154	database.
155	
156	**You changed something and the struct still shows the old value.** Loaders do not refresh. Re-fetch
157	the issue.
158	
159	**Pull requests show up on the issues page, or a count is too high.** A query missing the `IsPull`
160	condition.
161	
162	**You looked up issue `#42` and got somebody else's issue.** You used the URL number as an `ID`.
163	Match repository plus index.
164	
165	**A test you did not touch fails on a consistency check.** The repository row stores counts —
166	`NumIssues`, `NumClosedIssues`, `NumPulls` and friends — alongside the real issues. Changing issue
167	state, or adding a fixture row, means keeping those in step.
168	
169	**You grouped the list by category and a group appears twice, or in a different place, on page 2.**
170	The grouping is worked out in two places that must agree: `applyGroupByLabelScope` in
171	`models/issues/issue_search.go` sorts the rows in SQL so that one page's issues of the same category
172	sit together, and `GroupByExclusiveLabelScope` in `models/issues/issue_group.go` then cuts that page
173	into groups in Go. If you change the order in one, change it in the other. In particular both settle
174	ties on the label's `id`, not its name, because the database and Go do not sort text the same way.
175	
176	**`Test_MigrateFromGiteaToGitea` fails with "missing fixture" after you add a column to `Issue`.** The
177	migration code fetches issues in pages sized by `db.MaxBatchInsertSize` (`models/db/engine.go`): 999
178	divided by the number of columns. One more column changes the page size, the request asks for a
179	different `limit`, and the recorded response in
180	`tests/integration/_mock_data/Test_MigrateFromGiteaToGitea/` no longer matches its name. Rename that
181	file to the new `limit`; its contents stay valid while the repository has fewer issues than the page size.
182	
183	**Building an issue's link crashes with a nil pointer.** `Issue.Link()` reads `issue.Repo`, and
184	`GetIssueByID` does not fill it in. Call `LoadRepo(ctx)` first.
185	
186	**You go looking for pull requests in `models/pull` and it is nearly empty.** Pull requests are in
187	`models/issues/pull.go`. `models/pull` only holds automerge and review state. Both `Issue` and
188	`PullRequest` also carry an `Index`; they agree, and you should write through the issue.
189	
190	## Where to go next
191	
192	- `docs/models-issues.md` (in this folder) — the reference page this was written from
193	- `models-db.md` — transactions and the numbering helper
194	- `models-repo-and-git.md` — those counter columns, and the per-repo feature switches

Your local `main` matches the remote (`94dfae067e`). I've built Issue #14 on `feature/issue-14-milestone-burndown` and tested it, but none of it is committed, since your hook leaves commits to you. Firefox e2e fails on this machine for the existing #13 tests too, so I could only verify the browser tests in Chromium. I followed the plan in `arjun-notes/claude_issue14.md`, taking decisions D1–D7 as recommended.

**What it does:** the milestone page now shows a burndown chart under the progress bar, with four lines:
- **Remaining:** open items per day.
- **Total in milestone:** a faint dashed line, so added scope is visible.
- **Ideal:** dashed, from the first day with work down to zero on the due date.
- **Projected finish:** dotted, from today's remaining work down to zero.

A one-line summary above the chart says in words whether the milestone is on track, late or done, and the canvas carries it as its screen-reader label. The chart loads from its own endpoint, `/milestone/{id}/burndown`, which has the same access rules as the milestone page.

**Changes from the plan** (also recorded in the plan file):
- The ideal line starts on the first day the milestone has anything in it, not the day it was created. Otherwise a milestone created empty and filled the next day draws a flat line at zero.
- A closed milestone's chart runs to its close date, or later if items changed after it closed, so today's count always matches the progress bar.
- A due date more than a year past the chart is treated as no due date for charting, so the test data's year-9999 date doesn't stretch the axis.
- I added two summary strings: one for a projection with no due date, and one for finishing exactly on the due date, instead of "0 days before".
- I fixed one bug the e2e test caught: two nested elements were both announced as images to screen readers.

**Verification:**
- **Tests:** unit tests for the database queries, the burndown calculation and the frontend logic, plus integration and Chromium e2e tests, all pass. The calculation tests pass under both UTC and New York time and include both daylight-saving changes. Deliberately breaking the close handling made 3 of them fail.
- **Linters:** the Go linter, ESLint and the TypeScript checker are clean.
- **Docs:** `check.sh` passes when run from the fixed copy on `fix/check-sh-bash32`. This branch still has the old script that crashes on macOS bash.
- **Commit order:** I replayed the Go commits one at a time into a throwaway checkout, and each builds in order.
- **Screenshot:** I took one to confirm the layout and switched the legend to line-style entries.

/Users/asb/.claude/settings.json
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# personal-config v0.7.0 · 2026-10-03 · config cc3563fc · standard v1.2.0
# PreToolUse guard: refuses the git commands the owner reserved for themselves.
# Exit 2 is the code Claude Code treats as "blocked, tell the model why" — stderr reaches the
# model, so the message is the ritual it should follow instead.
#
# Two rules about how this reads a payload, both learned by being wrong:
#   1. The command is parsed out of the JSON, never pattern-matched out of the raw payload. The
#      payload also carries the tool's *description*, so a plain `ls` was blocked whenever its
#      description said "git commit".
#   2. The command's words are walked, not substring-matched. `grep "git commit" PASSOFF.md`
#      writes nothing and was blocked; `git -C . commit -m x` writes a commit and passed.
#
# macOS ships bash 3.2, so nothing here uses associative arrays or `${x^^}`.
set -euo pipefail

payload="$(cat)"

if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  cmd="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty')"
else
  # Fail closed. Over-blocking costs one message; a commit the owner did not make cannot be
  # taken back from a shared checkout.
  echo "commit guard: jq not found — falling back to matching the whole payload." >&2
  cmd="$payload"
fi

# Wrappers whose own arguments are the real command. `sh`/`bash` are here so `sh -c "git push"`
# is still caught; the de-quoted second pass below is what makes that reach the word `git`.
is_wrapper() {
  case "$1" in
    env | sudo | nohup | time | xargs | sh | bash | zsh | dash | ksh) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

is_blocked() {
  local -a words=()
  read -r -a words <<<"$1" || true
  local n=${#words[@]}
```

Here's everything, with exact names taken from a fresh run just now. One correction first: last time I said there were 49 tests. That number was wrong; the actual count is below.

## Tests I added

Every one of these passes as of this run. The e2e tests last passed in Chromium after the final change that affects them.

**1. Database queries:** `models/issues/milestone_history_test.go` (3 tests, 2 subtests)
- `TestGetMilestoneScopeEvents`: returns only this milestone's join and leave records, in time order with ties broken by insertion order. It excludes other milestones, other repos and other comment kinds.
- `TestGetMilestoneStateEvents`: returns close, merge and reopen records in order and skips plain comments.
  - `/Chunked`: 1,200 issue IDs, split into batches, still return every record in the right order.
  - `/NoIssues`: an empty list returns nothing.
- `TestGetMilestoneItems`: the PR in milestone 1 is returned (D1). Issues that have left are included once, and an issue from another repo can't leak in.

**2. Burndown calculation:** `services/issue/milestone_burndown_test.go` (22 cases, plus a timezone test with 2 subtests)
- `TestCalcMilestoneBurndown` covers:
  - no items
  - steady burn to done on the due date
  - scope creep
  - an item leaving the milestone
  - reopen
  - merged PR
  - an item added already closed
  - each of the missing-history fallbacks (no join record, first record is a move out, no close record, no close time)
  - the database winning when the records disagree with it
  - a milestone with no creation time
  - both closed-milestone endings (on the close day, or later if items changed after closing)
  - late, early and two-week-window projections
  - too little history to project
  - due date on or before the first day of work
  - due date in the year 9999
  - records for unrelated issues being ignored

  Every case also asserts that the last point matches the items' current state.
- `TestCalcMilestoneBurndownTimezone`: the same events land on different dates in UTC and New York.
  - `/DSTEnds` and `/DSTStarts`: no date is skipped or duplicated across daylight-saving changes, and a due date stored at 23:59:59 local time stays on its own day.

**3. Frontend logic:** `RepoMilestoneBurndown.utils.test.ts` (5 tests)
- `formatLocale`
- `burndownSummary`: every status, including late, on the due date, and early.
- `idealLine`
- `projectionLine`
- `burndownAxisMax`

**4. Endpoint integration:** `tests/integration/milestone_burndown_test.go` (5 subtests)
- `Data`: a milestone and issues created through the API produce the right counts and ideal line, and the counts match the progress bar.
- `RealLifecycle` (added this round): real close, reopen and move actions write the history records the chart reads. Counts in both milestones are correct.
- `CountsPullRequests` (added this round): PRs count, and a year-9999 due date draws no ideal line.
- `NotFound`: an unknown milestone, or another repo's milestone, returns 404.
- `PrivateRepoHidden`: signed-out readers of a private repo get 404.

**5. Browser e2e:** `tests/e2e/milestone-burndown.test.ts` (2 tests), plus two helpers in `tests/e2e/utils.ts`
- `milestone burndown charts remaining work against the ideal line`: the canvas renders, the summary text and screen-reader label are present, and there are no JS errors.
- `milestone burndown shows an empty state without items`.

That's 37 cases in all (3 + 22 + 3 + 5 + 2), or 41 counting subtests.

## Other runs I did

- **Baseline on clean `main`** before any changes: `go build ./...`, `models/issues`, `services/issue` (UTC and New York), and the milestone integration tests all passed.
- **Regression after the changes:** full `models/issues` and `services/issue` packages, and every integration test with "Milestone" in its name.
- **Existing e2e tests next to mine** (Chromium): `milestone.test.ts` and `repo-issues-chart.test.ts` pass. In Firefox, those existing tests fail with API timeouts just like mine, so it's this machine, not the feature.
- **Deliberate-breakage checks:** breaking the close handling failed 3 calculation tests, and dropping reopen records from the query failed `RealLifecycle`. Both originals were restored.
- **Linters:** golangci-lint (0 issues after 5 modernize fixes), ESLint, `vue-tsc`, `make fmt`, a trailing-whitespace scan, and `check.sh` run from the fixed copy.
- **Commit-order check:** I replayed commits 1–3 one at a time into a throwaway checkout, and each built in order.
- **Visual check:** two screenshots from a temporary Playwright test, since deleted. This led to the legend fix.

**Known gaps:**
- A real PR merge isn't tested end to end, only in the calculation tests.
- The Vue component has no direct test; its logic is in the tested `.utils.ts` file.
- Each e2e test takes about 3 seconds against the 2-second target, the same as the existing chart tests.

## Commits, in order, and why

Splitting it this way gives one layer per commit, so each can be reviewed and reverted on its own, and each builds on the one before.

1. **`feat(issues): read milestone scope and state history (#14)`**: `milestone_history.go` and its test. This is the database layer by itself. It's the only commit that touches queries, so a reviewer can check the join and batching for performance in isolation, and nothing above it can be correct unless this is.

2. **`feat(milestone): compute a burndown with an ideal line and projected finish (#14)`**: `milestone_burndown.go` and its test. This is the risky logic: rebuilding history, the fallbacks, dates and projection. Keeping it separate means the tests that prove it sit right next to it. It depends only on commit 1.

3. **`feat(milestone): serve burndown data for a milestone (#14)`**: the handler in `routers/web/repo/milestone.go`, the route in `routers/web/web.go`, and the integration test. This is where the feature becomes reachable, so it's the commit where permissions get reviewed. The integration test belongs here because it exercises this route.

4. **`feat(milestone): chart the burndown on the milestone page (#14)`**: the locale strings, the template mount point, `index.ts` registration, the feature entry point, the Vue component, and the utils file with its test. This is everything visible to users. It's one commit because none of these pieces does anything without the others.

5. **`test(e2e): cover the milestone burndown chart (#14)`**: `tests/e2e/utils.ts` (the new helpers) and the e2e test. It's test-only, so AGENTS.md calls for the `test` type. It comes after 4 because it needs the page to exist.

6. **`docs(context): note where milestone history lives (#14)`**: two reference pages and their two guides. MAINTENANCE.md rule 12 asks for the `docs(context)` type, and each reference page and its guide have to land together or `check.sh` reports drift.

Every commit:
- ends its subject with `(#14)`, as AGENTS.md now requires,
- carries `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5`,
- has no `Co-Authored-By`, and
- names its files explicitly, so the `.gitignore` typo and the stray untracked files stay out.

**Outside this branch:** the `check.sh` fix on `fix/check-sh-bash32`, as `fix(context): let check.sh run under macos bash 3.2`. It doesn't belong in the #14 PR because it fixes a separate bug that affects everyone on macOS. It needs an issue number before it meets the new subject rule.

The copyable `git add` / `git commit` commands are in my previous two messages. Step 3 is the version from my last message, which includes the new integration tests.

`.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` is gone from your machine, and git no longer lists it as a change. It remains in the repository for teammates who use it.

- **How:** I set git's skip-worktree flag on the file. That changes your local git index only; there's no commit and nothing to push, so your branch's six commits are untouched.

- **One catch:** if someone changes that file on `main`, a later pull or branch switch may stop with an error about it. Running the undo command above clears it.

```text
## Current sprint: Sprint 1

- **Dates:** Sep 22 – Oct 8, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 8, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100 (10% of the course grade).
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D6) or no release (D7) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** every Sprint 0 standard and convention still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 1` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue | 7 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs | 36 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 7 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint1/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint1/report.md` |
| D7 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s1` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D8 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Every issue has exactly **one** assignee. Specs should be final by
  Sep 27.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. The folder must exist even if no AI was used. In
  that case, post an issue comment saying so. Log links go in **issue comments only**, never in PRs
  (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D7:** keep Sprint 0's base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s0` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s1`), push the tag
  to origin, and write release notes listing the features, fixes and improvements.
- **Reviews:** each student reviews at least one PR per sprint. Over the semester, each student
  reviews every teammate at least once.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR accepted by upstream Gitea.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.

  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

---
## Summary
A Gitea milestone page shows only a progress bar and the current open/closed counts. There's no way to see how work progressed over the milestone's life, whether the team is on track for the due date, or when scope was added mid-way.

This feature adds a **burndown chart** to the milestone page: the number of open issues from the milestone's **creation to its due date**, compared against an **ideal line**, with markers for scope changes and a **projected finish date** based on the current pace.

It helps teams running sprints or releases (like our own course sprints) spot early when a milestone is slipping, and helps leads explain *why* — for example, because issues were added partway through.

## User story
As a team lead, I want a burndown chart for each milestone comparing actual progress against an ideal pace so that I can tell early whether we'll finish by the due date and see when scope changed.

## Proposed behavior

### Chart
Shown on the milestone page (`/{owner}/{repo}/milestone/{id}`) above the issue list, collapsible.

- **X-axis:** milestone creation date → due date (extended to today if the milestone is overdue).
- **Actual line:** number of open items in the milestone at the end of each day.
- **Ideal line:** a straight line from the open count at the milestone's start down to 0 at the due date.
- **Scope-change markers:** points where items were **added to** or **removed from** the milestone (explains why the actual line goes *up*).
- **Projected finish:** a dashed trend line from the recent burn rate, with a label such as "At this pace: Oct 3". Hidden when there's not enough data or nothing has closed yet.
- **Hover details:** for each day, list which items were closed, reopened, added, or removed (with links).
- **Include pull requests toggle:** off by default (issues only); when on, PRs in the milestone are counted too. The choice is kept in the URL (e.g. `?include_pulls=1`) so it can be shared.

### Accurate history
Counts are rebuilt by replaying each item's timeline, not from the current state:
- issue created (only counts once it's in the milestone)
- closed (`CommentTypeClose`) and reopened (`CommentTypeReopen`) events
- milestone changes (`CommentTypeMilestone`, which records the old and new milestone), so items moved between milestones are counted only while they belonged to this one
- merged PRs count as closed when the pull request toggle is on

### Edge cases
- **No due date:** show the actual line and scope markers from creation to today; hide the ideal line and projection, with a note explaining why.
- **Due date changed:** use the current due date for the ideal line.
- **Overdue milestone:** extend the X-axis to today; the ideal line still ends at the due date.
- **Closed milestone:** the chart ends at the milestone's close date.
- **Item added after it was already closed:** changes the total but not the open count.
- **Empty milestone:** show an empty-state message instead of a chart.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The milestone page shows a burndown chart from creation to due date with actual and ideal lines.
- [ ] History is rebuilt from timeline events, so reopened items and items moved between milestones are counted correctly.
- [ ] Scope additions and removals are marked on the chart.
- [ ] A projected finish date is shown when there's enough data, and hidden otherwise.
- [ ] Hovering a day lists the items that changed that day.
- [ ] The "Include pull requests" toggle is off by default, changes the counts when turned on, and is reflected in the URL.
- [ ] All edge cases above behave as described.
- [ ] Users without permission to read the milestone's issues/PRs cannot see the chart or its data endpoint, and private items are never leaked in hover details.
- [ ] All new UI strings are in `locale_en-US.json`.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the timeline replay (close/reopen, add/remove/move between milestones, add-after-closed, PR toggle) and the ideal/projection calculations.

## Implementation notes
- Milestone dates are on `models/issues/milestone.go` (`CreatedUnix`, `DeadlineUnix`, `ClosedDateUnix`); it currently stores only current counts (`NumIssues`, `NumClosedIssues`), so history must come from comments.
- Timeline event types are defined in `models/issues/comment.go` (`CommentTypeReopen` = 1, `CommentTypeClose` = 2, `CommentTypeMilestone` = 8, with `OldMilestoneID` / `MilestoneID`).
- Milestone page: `routers/web/repo/milestone.go` (`MilestoneIssuesAndPulls`) and `templates/repo/issue/milestone_issues.tmpl`. A JSON data endpoint like the Activity charts' `/data` routes (`routers/web/web.go:1608-1618`) keeps page load fast.
- Frontend can follow the Chart.js pattern in `web_src/js/components/RepoCodeFrequency.vue` / `RepoContributors.vue`.
- Related to #13 (Activity tab issues chart) but **independent** — neither requires the other. If #13 has already merged, reuse its chart component where it fits.

## Rough scope
**Large.** The core is an accurate timeline-replay engine across close, reopen, and milestone-move events, plus scope-change detection, projection math, a PR toggle, many edge cases, permission checks, a new data endpoint, a chart UI, and thorough tests — more than a single sprint of work.

## Source
Personal use and our team's workflow: we plan work in fixed-length sprints with due dates, and a burndown chart is the standard way scrum teams track whether a sprint is on track. Also a gap compared to tools like Jira and GitLab, which offer milestone burndown charts.

  await page.waitForTimeout(300);
  await chart.screenshot({path: '$SP/markers-hover.png'});
  await apiDeleteRepo(page.request, user, repoName);
});
EOF

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 19:23:45Z)**_

Scope additions and removals are now marked on the chart, and all checks pass. I also fixed two bugs in the original chart that the markers exposed. Nothing is committed yet; the commands are below.

**What the chart shows now:**
- **Markers.** A ▲ on the "Total in milestone" line on any day items were added, and a ▼ on any day items were removed. The shapes carry the meaning, so it doesn't depend on colour. The first day of work isn't marked: what the milestone starts with is its plan, not a change.
- **Hover.** Hovering anywhere snaps to the nearest day and lists everything on that date, e.g. "2026-01-09: Added to milestone: 2, Remaining: 6, Total in milestone: 7".
- **Visibility.** The total line was too faint to read the markers against, so it now uses a mid-grey from the theme, which every theme defines. I checked it in light and dark.

**Bugs I fixed along the way:**
- **The line moved a day early.** Each change appeared the day before it happened, which I confirmed against Chart.js's source. It now steps on the actual day, lined up with the markers.
- **Hover only worked right on a date.** The tooltip fired within about 6px of a date point, so hovering between days showed nothing.

**What I'll build next.** Push back on any of this before I start:

- **Permissions first.** The chart will only ever count and list items the viewer can read: issues need issue access, and PRs need PR access. The server enforces this, so it can't be bypassed from the browser.
- **"Include pull requests" toggle:**
  - The endpoint takes `?include_pulls=1`, and the default is issues only.
  - The checkbox reads and writes `include_pulls` in the page URL without dropping the issue list's own filter parameters.
  - It's hidden for viewers who can't read PRs.
- **Hover details:**
  - Each day carries its list of changes: closed (merges count as closed), reopened, added and removed.
  - A canvas tooltip can't hold clickable links, so the list renders below the chart for the day you're hovering. It stays put while you move your mouse down to click a link.
  - It starts on the most recent day with changes, so it's useful without hovering. Titles are escaped by Vue.
- **Collapsible:** the chart sits in a `<details>` element, open by default, so it's keyboard-accessible with no extra JavaScript.
- **Tests:** the permission and toggle checks at the integration level, change lists in the calculation tests, URL and list logic in Vitest, and an e2e test covering the toggle, collapse and a "Closed" link.

85	func (s burndownState) diff(next burndownState, at int64) burndownDelta {
86		r0, s0 := s.counts()
87		r1, s1 := next.counts()
88		return burndownDelta{at: at, remaining: r1 - r0, scope: s1 - s0}
89	}
90	
91	// replayMilestoneItem turns one item's comments into changes to the milestone's counts. Missing history
92	// is filled in so the replay always ends where the database is now: an item in the milestone with no
93	// comment saying it joined (migrated issues have none) joins when it was created or the milestone was,
94	// and a closed item with no close comment closes at its closed_unix.
95	func replayMilestoneItem(item issues_model.MilestoneItem, events []issues_model.MilestoneEvent, milestoneID, milestoneCreated int64) []burndownDelta {
96		events = slices.Clone(events) // synthetic events are appended below
97		created := int64(item.CreatedUnix)
98		var firstScope *issues_model.MilestoneEvent
99		hasClose := false
100		for i := range events {
101			switch events[i].Type {
102			case issues_model.CommentTypeMilestone:
103				if firstScope == nil {
104					firstScope = &events[i]
105				}
106			case issues_model.CommentTypeClose, issues_model.CommentTypeMergePull:
107				hasClose = true
108			}
109		}
110	
111		// synthetic events take id 0 so they sort before a real comment in the same second
112		joinAt := max(created, milestoneCreated)
113		if firstScope == nil && item.MilestoneID == milestoneID {
114			events = append(events, issues_model.MilestoneEvent{Type: issues_model.CommentTypeMilestone, MilestoneID: milestoneID, CreatedUnix: timeutil.TimeStamp(joinAt)})
115		} else if firstScope != nil && firstScope.MilestoneID != milestoneID {
116			// its first recorded move is out of the milestone, so it was in it before then
117			joinAt = min(joinAt, int64(firstScope.CreatedUnix))
118			events = append(events, issues_model.MilestoneEvent{Type: issues_model.CommentTypeMilestone, MilestoneID: milestoneID, CreatedUnix: timeutil.TimeStamp(joinAt)})
119		}
120		if item.IsClosed && !hasClose {
121			// a close time of zero predates the item, so clamp it as the Activity issues chart does
122			closedAt := max(int64(item.ClosedUnix), created)
123			events = append(events, issues_model.MilestoneEvent{Type: issues_model.CommentTypeClose, CreatedUnix: timeutil.TimeStamp(closedAt)})
124		}
125		slices.SortFunc(events, issues_model.CompareMilestoneEvents)
126	
127		state := burndownState{open: true}
128		lastAt := created
129		deltas := make([]burndownDelta, 0, len(events)+1)
130		for _, e := range events {
131			next := state
132			switch e.Type {
133			case issues_model.CommentTypeMilestone:
134				if e.MilestoneID == milestoneID {
135					next.inScope = true
136				} else if e.OldMilestoneID == milestoneID {
137					next.inScope = false
138				}
139			case issues_model.CommentTypeClose, issues_model.CommentTypeMergePull:
140				next.open = false
141			case issues_model.CommentTypeReopen:
142				next.open = true
143			}
144			lastAt = max(lastAt, int64(e.CreatedUnix))
145			if next != state {
146				deltas = append(deltas, state.diff(next, int64(e.CreatedUnix)))
147				state = next
148			}
149		}
150	
151		// the comments can still disagree with the row, for instance after a reopen whose close was never
152		// recorded, and the row is the truth the progress bar shows, so end on it
153		want := burndownState{inScope: item.MilestoneID == milestoneID, open: !item.IsClosed}
154		if state != want {
155			at := lastAt
156			if state.open && !want.open {
157				at = max(at, int64(item.ClosedUnix))
158			}
159			deltas = append(deltas, state.diff(want, at))
160		}
161		return deltas
162	}
163

const includePullsParam = 'include_pulls';

export function includePullsFromSearch(search: string): boolean {
  return new URLSearchParams(search).get(includePullsParam) === '1';
}

// the page's query with the toggle set or cleared, keeping the issue list's own filters intact
export function searchWithIncludePulls(search: string, includePulls: boolean): string {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(search);
  if (includePulls) {
    params.set(includePullsParam, '1');
  } else {
    params.delete(includePullsParam);
  }
  const query = params.toString();
  return query ? `?${query}` : '';
}

export function burndownDataUrl(link: string, includePulls: boolean): string {
  return includePulls ? `${link}?${includePullsParam}=1` : link;
}

export function changeLink(repoLink: string, change: BurndownChange): string {
  return `${repoLink}/${change.isPull ? 'pulls' : 'issues'}/${change.index}`;
}

export function changesOn(data: MilestoneBurndown, date: string): BurndownChange[] {
  return data.points.find((p) => p.date === date)?.changes ?? [];
}

// the list starts on the latest day anything changed, so it is useful before anyone hovers
export function latestChangeDate(data: MilestoneBurndown): string {
  return data.points.findLast((p) => p.changes !== undefined)?.date ?? '';
}

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import {login, apiCreateRepo, apiCreateIssue, apiCreateMilestone, apiDeleteRepo, assertNoJsError, randomString} from './utils.ts';

test('milestone burndown charts remaining work against the ideal line', async ({page}) => {
  const repoName = `e2e-burndown-${randomString(8)}`;
  const user = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
  await Promise.all([login(page), apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repoName})]);
  const dueOn = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
  const {id} = await apiCreateMilestone(page.request, {owner: user, repo: repoName, title: 'Sprint', dueOn});
  await Promise.all([
    apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner: user, repo: repoName, title: 'First', milestone: id}),
    apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner: user, repo: repoName, title: 'Second', milestone: id}),
  ]);

  await page.goto(`/${user}/${repoName}/milestone/${id}`);
  const chart = page.locator('#milestone-burndown-chart');
  await expect(chart.locator('canvas')).toBeVisible();
  // one day of history is too little to project, and the summary says so in words
  await expect(chart.locator('.milestone-burndown-summary')).toContainText('two days of history');
  await expect(chart.locator('canvas')).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', /two days of history/);

  await assertNoJsError(page);
  await apiDeleteRepo(page.request, user, repoName);
});

All three pieces are built and verified, and issue #14's acceptance criteria are now all covered. Nothing is committed; your markers work is folded into these commits since it was still uncommitted.

**Hover details**
- The server now returns each day's list of changes: closed (merged PRs count as closed), reopened, added and removed, with each item's number and title. Days with no changes leave the list out.
- A chart tooltip can't hold clickable links, so the list appears under the chart for the day you hover. It stays put while you move the mouse down to click a link, and before you hover it shows the latest day with changes.
- Additions on the first day aren't listed, matching the markers; closes on that day are.

**"Include pull requests" toggle**
- The chart counts issues only by default. Turning the checkbox on adds `include_pulls=1` to the page URL without touching the issue list's own filters, and it survives a reload. This reverses my earlier "always count PRs" decision.
- The server only counts and lists kinds the viewer can read: issues need issue access, PRs need PR access. The checkbox is also hidden from viewers who can't read PRs.
- Two new integration tests each switch off one repo unit (issues or pull requests) and confirm nothing leaks. With the permission check bypassed, both tests fail.

**Collapsible**
- The chart sits under a "Burndown" heading with a rotating chevron, the same pattern as the grouped issue list. Clicking the heading collapses it; the summary line stays visible.

**Also fixed:** "…two days of historySet a due date…" was missing a space whenever a milestone had no due date. It now reads "…history · Set a due date to see the ideal line".

**Verified:**
- **Go:** tests in both timezones, the integration tests, and golangci-lint for Linux and Windows (after one fix: Gitea bans `encoding/json` in favour of `modules/json`).
- **Frontend:** ESLint, stylelint, `vue-tsc`, and the full Vitest suite (280 tests).
- **E2E:** all 5 Chromium tests pass. The main burndown test now takes about 3 seconds, over the 2-second target.
- **Docs:** `check.sh` passes. `services-issue.md` and its guide now say callers must leave out kinds the viewer can't read.
- **Commit order:** the Go slices build in order.
- **Visual:** screenshots of the change list, hovering, and collapsing.

export function changeTooltipLines(changes: BurndownChange[], labels: Record<BurndownChange['kind'], string>, moreTemplate: string): string[] {

## What to log

Every AI session tied to this project: code, debugging, tests, reviews, drafting issues and PRs,
design discussion, the sprint report. That includes sessions that went nowhere. Purely academic
questions unrelated to the project don't need logging.

## Structure

```
ai-logs/
  sprint1/
    <github-username>/                          ← exact GitHub username, matching case
      .gitkeep                                  ← the folder must exist even if you used no AI
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>/           ← attachments (images, etc.), optional
```

Team folders: `ab-wm`, `arjunsb26`, `CarsonRackley`, `controlled-opposition`, `Jack-Donohue`,
`vvchopra`.

## Naming

`YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`

- **Date:** the day the session started.
- **Sprint folder:** the sprint that date falls in, not the sprint the work is for.
- **Tool:** one of the course identifiers: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`,
  `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Claude Code run inside VS Code is
  `claude-code`.
- **Slug:** lowercase words joined with hyphens that say what the session did. Put the issue number
  first when there is one: `issue-52-impl`, `issue-52-spec`, `pr-61-review`, `sprint1-report`.
  Replace auto-generated slugs such as `local-command-caveat...`.
- **Formats:** `.md` is preferred; `.txt` and `.json` are also accepted. No `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.html`
  or share links.

## Capturing a session

| Tool | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code (terminal or VS Code), other agentic CLIs | Start it with [SpecStory](https://specstory.com/): `specstory run claude`, from the repo root. Forgot? Run `specstory sync` afterwards; it back-fills from Claude Code's local history. Then copy from `.specstory/history/` (git-ignored) into your folder and rename it to the convention. |
| Web chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini, ...) | Install a browser chat exporter and export the session as Markdown right after it ends. Include any files you pasted in as context. |
| Claude Desktop | SpecStory doesn't capture it. Copy the conversation into a `.md` file by hand. |

At the end of each sprint, run `specstory sync` once more and re-copy. A log copied mid-session is
incomplete.

## Content

- The **tool and AI model** used (SpecStory writes both).
- The **complete** prompt and response history. For agentic tools, that includes file edits and
  commands (SpecStory includes them). Logs with missing responses or truncated histories are
  **invalid**. Don't hand-write, summarise or trim a log; only rename it.

Closes #14

## What changed

The milestone page (`/{owner}/{repo}/milestone/{id}`) now has a burndown chart above the issue list, folded under a "Burndown" heading that collapses. It shows:

- **Remaining:** open items at the end of each day, stepping on the day each change happened.
- **Total in milestone:** a dashed line with ▲ where items were added and ▼ where they were removed. The milestone's first day of work is its plan, so it is not marked.
- **Ideal:** a straight line from the first day with work down to zero on the due date.
- **Projected finish:** a dotted line extrapolated from the net burn rate over the last 14 days. A one-line summary says in words whether that is early, on the due date or late, or why there is no projection yet.
- **Hover details:** hovering a day lists the items that changed on it (closed, reopened, added, removed; a merge counts as closed). The same list appears under the chart with a link to each item, since links can't be clicked inside a canvas tooltip. It starts on the latest day with changes.
- **Include pull requests:** a checkbox, off by default, kept in the page URL as `include_pulls=1` without disturbing the issue list's own filters.

History is rebuilt from timeline comments (milestone changes, closes, merges and reopens), not from the current state. There is no schema change and no migration. The chart loads from its own endpoint, `GET /{owner}/{repo}/milestone/{id}/burndown`, so the issue list stays as fast as before.

## Why

A milestone page shows only a progress bar, so there is no way to tell whether a milestone is on track, when scope changed, or when it will finish. Acceptance criteria, in the order the issue lists them:

- **AC1** (chart with actual and ideal lines): the remaining and ideal lines. The axis runs from the first day to whichever is latest of today, the due date and the projection.
- **AC2** (history rebuilt from timeline events): each item's milestone, close, merge and reopen comments are replayed. Issues migrated in without those comments fall back to their row, and the replay always ends on the database's current state, so today's count matches the progress bar.
- **AC3** (scope additions and removals marked): ▲ and ▼ on the total line.
- **AC4** (projection shown only with enough data): hidden with under two days of history, when nothing has burned down over the window, when the work is done, or when the milestone is closed.
- **AC5** (hovering a day lists what changed): in the tooltip, and repeated with links under the chart.
- **AC6** (pull request toggle, off by default, in the URL): `include_pulls=1`; the checkbox reads it on load and writes it on change.
- **AC7** (edge cases): no due date hides the ideal line and says why; a changed due date uses the current one; an overdue milestone runs to today; a closed milestone ends on its close date (or on a later change, so the last point still matches the counters); an item added already closed widens the total but not the remaining count; an empty milestone shows a message instead of a chart.
- **AC8** (no access without permission, nothing private leaked): the endpoint sits in the same route group, with the same guards, as the milestone page. The milestone pages let in anyone who can read issues *or* pull requests, so the server counts and lists a kind only if the viewer can read it, and the checkbox is hidden from viewers who can't read pull requests.
- **AC9** (strings in `locale_en-US.json`): every visible string is under `repo.milestones.burndown.*`.
- **AC10** (unit tests for replay, toggle, ideal and projection): see below.

Deliberate differences from the issue's wording:
- The ideal line starts on the **first day with work**, not the creation day. Otherwise a milestone created empty and filled the next day draws a flat line at zero.
- A due date more than a year past the chart is not drawn. The test fixtures' year-9999 due date would otherwise flatten the chart.

## How it was tested

- **Go unit tests** (`models/issues/milestone_history_test.go`, `services/issue/milestone_burndown_test.go`):
  - The calculation is a pure function that takes `now` and a time zone, so 23 table cases cover every replay path: scope creep, items leaving, reopen, merge, an item added already closed, each fallback for missing history, the database winning when comments disagree, both closed-milestone endings, late, early and windowed projections, and the ideal line's limits.
  - Every case also asserts that the last point matches the items' current state.
  - Separate tests cover the per-day change lists, and dates across the New York daylight-saving changes.
  - The query tests check that only this milestone's and repository's history is read, that events come back in order, and that the batched lookups return every row.
- **Integration tests** (`tests/integration/milestone_burndown_test.go`):
  - `RealLifecycle` closes, reopens and moves issues through the real API and checks the history records Gitea actually wrote. The final counts alone can't show that, because the replay ends on the database's state either way.
  - `PullRequestsOnRequest` checks the toggle.
  - Two tests switch off the issues unit or the pull request unit and check that nothing of that kind is counted or listed. Both were confirmed to fail when the permission check is removed.
  - The rest check not-found and private-repository access.
- **Vitest** (`RepoMilestoneBurndown.utils.test.ts`): the summary sentence, ideal and projection lines, scope markers, axis range, tooltip lines, URL handling for the toggle (the issue list's filters survive it) and item links.
- **E2E** (`tests/e2e/milestone-burndown.test.ts`): the chart renders with its summary and accessible label; a closed issue appears in the change list with the right link; the toggle starts off, writes the URL, survives a reload and clears; the chart collapses and expands; an empty milestone shows its message.
- **Checked by hand,** because canvas drawing and multi-day history can't be produced through the API in real time: screenshots against a synthetic two-week history (markers, tooltip contents, step timing, the change list while moving the pointer to it), in light and dark themes, open and collapsed.

## Design

See the Design Decision in #14: history is rebuilt from timeline comments when the chart is requested, rather than stored as daily snapshots. Later changes are listed under Why.

```markdown
## Design Decision
**Decision:** Rebuild each milestone's history when the chart is requested, by replaying its items' timeline comments (milestone changes, closes, merges and reopens), and serve it from a separate JSON endpoint that the page loads after it renders.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- A daily snapshot table filled by a scheduled job, which the chart reads directly.
- Deriving the chart from each issue's current `created_unix` and `closed_unix`, as the Activity tab's issues chart (#13) does.

**Rationale:** Snapshots need a migration and a new scheduled job, and they only start recording on the day they ship, so every existing milestone would have no history. Current timestamps can't show an issue that was reopened, or one that moved between milestones, which the acceptance criteria require. Replaying comments works for every existing milestone straight away, needs no schema change, and is exact for anything Gitea recorded.

**Consequences:**
- The milestone columns on `comment` aren't indexed and `comment` has no `repo_id`. The query is bounded by the indexed comment type and a join on the repository's issues, and runs on its own lazy request so it can't slow the issue list.
- Issues migrated from other platforms have no milestone comments. The replay falls back to each issue's row and always ends on the database's current state, so the chart agrees with the progress bar.
- Dates are bucketed in the server's time zone, the zone due dates are stored in, so every viewer sees the same days.
- The milestone pages admit readers of issues *or* pull requests, so the endpoint has to filter by kind for each viewer. It does, and this is tested.

```

From now on, at the end of a piece of work, I'll remind you to run `specstory sync` and file the log, rather than to start sessions with `specstory run`.
